summary: Recent updates to Firefox's integration with WebRTC, the technology behind real-time video calls, involve several key improvements aimed at enhancing performance and maintainability. Notably, the platform decoder now correctly parses VP8 and VP9 quantization parameters, which helps with video quality assessments. The code has also transitioned from deprecated methods for frame dropping to more current practices, ensuring better stability during video playback. Additionally, several functions that create video encoders and decoders have been modified to use modern memory management techniques, returning smart pointers instead of raw pointers. These changes contribute to a more reliable and efficient video calling experience, reinforcing Firefox's commitment to high-quality media support in web applications.
